messages.subject: JRI and NAs in chars
messages.body_plain:
Dear Simon,

is there a way in JRI to distinguish between these two:

Rengine.eval("\"NA\"") // in R a char vector of length 1, which contains 
the string "NA" at pos 1
Rengine.eval("as.character(NA)") // in R a char vector of length 1, 
which contains a missing value at pos 1

It seems, that both get internally encoded as the same thing, namely the 
Java String "NA", but maybe I am wrong?

Best wishes,

Bernd

messages.subject: Rgui.exe does not terminate
messages.body_plain:
Dear list

I posted this question a few weeks ago, but haven't received a reply - 
any hints on where to start searching would be very helpful!

---------

I'm having a problem with rJava: Whenever I use my package that relies
on  rJava, Rgui.exe does not terminate properly. In other words, I load
my package, do some computations, close R, but an Rgui.exe process is
still listed in my process table and needs to be killed manually. My
suspicion is that the JVM initialized by rJava does not terminate
properly, but I don't know if this is really the case, and what to do
about it.

My system configuration: R 2.8.0, rJava 0.6, WinXP SP3, Java 1.6.0_07.

Any help would be much appreciated!

Best
Nils
-- 
Nils B. Weidmann
International Conflict Research
ETH Zurich
http://www.icr.ethz.ch/people/weidmann

messages.subject: Re: Rgui.exe does not terminate
messages.body_plain:
Hello list

Just the push the question: I had the same error. rJava does not terminate
correctly until the father java thread has been terminated. So I had to
keep the rJava thread open, catch it in a do-nothing-loop and clean the
workspace from time to time.

Btw: my system has the same configuration as yours.

regards,

Steffen

messages.subject_clean: R graphics won't refresh using plot(x)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I'm producing graphs/plots using the following code as an example (re =
org.rosuda.JRI.Rengine):

#code starts
re.eval ("library (ape)");
re.eval ("tree_mr <- nj(r_matrix)");
re.eval ("plot(tree_mr)");
#code ends

The graph is produced and looks fine, but if I reduce the graph to a
minimised icon and then maximise it, the graph is blank. The same thing
happens if I move another window across the graph - wherever the window
moves over the graph it appears to 'rub out' that part of the graph as
the image below the window does not re-appear once exposed again.

I'm using JDK 1.6, JRI 0.4.1 and R version 2.7.2 Patched (2008-09-02
r46484) on Linux.
If I run the code outside of JRI (e.g. through the R command line
interface), the graphics behave properly.

I was wondering if anyone had run into this problem before or if anyone
had any suggestions.

Merry Christmas and thanks for any help.
Best wishes,
Graham Etherington

messages.subject: Re: JRI and NAs in chars
messages.body_plain:
On Dec 11, 2008, at 13:45 , Bernd Bischl wrote:

> Dear Simon,
>
> is there a way in JRI to distinguish between these two:
>
> Rengine.eval("\"NA\"") // in R a char vector of length 1, which  
> contains
> the string "NA" at pos 1
> Rengine.eval("as.character(NA)") // in R a char vector of length 1,
> which contains a missing value at pos 1
>
> It seems, that both get internally encoded as the same thing, namely  
> the Java String "NA", but maybe I am wrong?
>

Yes, because they *are* the same in R:

 > charToRaw(as.character(NA))
[1] 4e 41
 > charToRaw("NA")
[1] 4e 41

So in terms of the content both "NA" and as.character(NA) are  
equivalent. R uses a trick to distinguish the two by creating a "NA"  
string on startup and then comparing the pointer address to determine  
whether a given "NA" is to be interpreted as NA or "NA". You cannot do  
that on Java side, since there are no pointers.

In theory JRI could use a similar trick internally and re-map the  
value, but I'm reluctant to use it, because the only unambiguous  
representation I can think of in Java would be null and that could  
break existing programs which assume that R strings are always non- 
null (in fact internal JRI code makes that assumption too, so  
implementing it would be a bit messy). Also this is no different from  
the approach used by int and double - they both have one specific  
numerical value that represents NAs, so strings are no different in  
that respect that "NA" is the special value there.

I'm not saying that it's set in stone - if there are compelling  
reasons, it could be changed - feel free to voice opinions.

Cheers,
Simon

> interface), the graphics behave properly.

> I was wondering if anyone had run into this problem before or if  
> anyone had any suggestions.

Apparently you're not running an event loop and/or you are using non- 
Java graphics. If you want an interactive environment (e.g. full  
console etc.), you should run the REPL - see startMainLoop() method  
and R documentation. Also you really don't want to use non-Java  
interactive graphics devices in JRI, because they don't integrate well  
with the UI, so  make sure you're using JavaGD (see JGR for details  
how to integrate everything seamlessly).

Cheers,
Simon

include Java sources, they have to be pre-compiled. The Java source  
code is, however, available from the SVN.

> check the contents. I just wonder if JGR is open source and if so,  
> how can I get the source. Thanks
>

Yes and yes (svn://svn.rforge.net/org/trunk/rosuda/JGR).

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: Fw: "Can't find R" error message
messages.body_plain:
Ravi,

the "can't find R" message usually means that you have uninstalled  
some R version after another was installed. Please re-install R and  
make sure the "save version number in registry" option is enabled  
during the installation (and you can take this opportunity to install  
R 2.8.1 ;)).

Cheers,
Simon
